seen_animation: A black-line apple with a leaf on its stem sits in front of grey scenery: a raised open hand on the left, fingers along the bottom right, and two long diagonal lines from the top. In frames 1-4 the apple drifts down and to the left until it overlaps the left hand. In frames 5-8 it sinks a little lower. In frames 9-12 it moves back to the right and up into the middle of the frame. In frames 12-16 a small dot appears low on the apple's body and grows into an x-shaped mark, while the stem and leaf get shorter and the apple sinks slightly. This reads as the apple being turned toward the viewer so its bottom (the blossom end) comes into view.
seen_film: Close shot of a man's two hands in front of a tweed jacket, holding an apple. In frames 1-4 the fingers turn the apple and dark spots on its skin come into view. In frames 5-8 the apple rolls down and to the left in the cupped hands, and the spotted side faces the camera. In frames 9-12 the hands bring the apple back to the right and the top of the apple turns toward the camera. In frames 13-16 the apple is turned further and lowered, and the blossom end at the bottom of the apple faces the camera between the fingers.
named_subject: An apple with a stem and one leaf (the doodle in c.png), turned in a pair of hands.
evidence: e.png 1-17: the apple drifts down-left toward the left hand, matching f.png 1-17 where the apple rolls down-left in the cupped hands. e.png 18-32: the apple moves back right and up toward frame centre, matching f.png 18-32. e.png 36-49: a dot appears at the apple's base (36-39), becomes an x (40-49) while the stem shortens (44-49) and the apple lowers, matching f.png 36-49 where the blossom end turns toward the camera and the apple drops. g.png shows one continuous arc down-left then back right with no gaps or reversals the film lacks. Outline size stays constant from e.png 1 to 49 apart from the slight squash at the end. I judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: Between e.png 1 and 35 the apple only slides; its stem stays upright and nothing on its surface moves, so the turning the film shows in that span (the spotted side rolling into view in f.png 5-20 and the top tilting toward camera in f.png 22-34) does not show up in the drawing until the x appears at e.png 36.
closes_when: Across e.png 5-35 the stem and leaf lean and shift off-centre as the apple rolls, and the x mark (or a few doodled spots) travels across the body from one edge, so the rotation starts when the film's does instead of only at the end.
protect: Keep the doodle's outline exactly as drawn (lumpy two-lobed bottom, leaf with one hatch line, single thin black stroke), the constant size, the down-left then back-right path timed to the film, the late x-shaped blossom end with the stem shortening, and the static grey hand scenery.
identity_gap: The character is the c.png apple in every frame; the only blemish is that grey left-hand scenery lines show through the apple body in e.png 9-17, which reads as lines crossing the drawing.
